key_insight: Deep learning PVS segmentation can look accurate on paper, yet only some models preserve the biological associations needed for trustworthy Alzheimer’s research.
clinical_relevance: For AD biomarker studies, model choice and local validation matter because external Dice alone may not reflect whether PVS measurements support correct downstream inference.
method: Benchmarked 5 open-source nnU-Net-based PVS segmentation models
Compared outputs to manual labels in 60 multi-site ADNI-3 scans and 12 VALDO challenge scans
Evaluated Dice at overall, voxel, object, and lesion levels, plus biomarker association validity
evidence_signal: ADNI-PVS-Net had the best internal Dice (0.58±0.14) but dropped to ≤0.11 externally, while only AD-trained models reproduced the expected PVS–amyloid relationship.
watch_item: Some models misclassified up to 32% of white matter hyperintensities as PVS, so cohort-specific manual validation is needed before clinical or research use.
paper_title: Examining the Clinical Utility of Deep Learning Models for Perivascular Space Segmentation in Alzheimer's Disease
